summary: Smith Mountain, in Bonner County near the Montana line, had a 1930 frame cabin, a 1934 pole tower and a 1965 concrete-block cab, sold and moved in 1975.

facts.design: Two-story concrete-block base with R-6 cab (1965); 10-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (1934)
facts.status_note: The cab was sold in 1975 and moved; an onX Offroad trail listing says the route ends at the remains of a lookout.

visit.trail_note: onX Offroad lists a 13-mile Smith Mountain route that ends at the remains of a lookout west of Troy, Montana.

events.note: A 10-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab was built.
The 1934 pole tower was sold for $2.
A two-story concrete-block lookout with an R-6 cab was built.
A July 6, 1966 newspaper item said Ernest Palin, a North Carolina student, would be the first Black lookout in the district at Smith Mountain. It describes a plan; it does not record that he served.
The cab was sold for $211 in 1975; Rex's page says the structure was sold and moved.

corrections.proposed: Two-story concrete-block base with R-6 cab (1965); the L-4 cab was on the 1934 pole tower
corrections.why: Sources tie the L-4 cab to the 1934 pole tower. The lookout standing until 1975 was the 1965 two-story structure with an R-6 cab.

corrections.proposed: Remove; no source gives a height for the 1965 cab, and the 10-foot figure belongs to the 1934 pole tower
corrections.why: A 10-foot pole tower was about 3 m, but it is not the structure the brief's record describes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not reconciled. FireLookout.com gives about 15 miles northeast of Hope; a 1967 newspaper item reprinted on Rex's page gives 10 miles south of Troy, Montana; the onX listing says west of Troy. The story gives the differing positions.

Not reconciled. FireLookout.com, the 1975 bid notice and Rex's page name the Kootenai National Forest; Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Kaniksu National Forest. The record keeps the brief's Kootenai, and the story notes the difference.
Not reconciled. The 1965 entry calls the cab concrete block; the 1975 bid notice describes it as wood on a cement block foundation.

Not reconciled. onX user status reports conflict: one dated Sep 20, 2026 marks the trail Open, and one dated May 17, 2025 marks it Obstructed by downed trees. These are not official notices, so no access level is recorded.

notes_for_editor: This is the Bonner County Smith Mountain. The Adams County Smith Mountain on the Payette National Forest (us-id-smith-mountain-2) is a different lookout with a different history, and search results mixed the two. Only the 1966 item names a staffer, and it describes a plan, not a record of service. No source supports an access level. The onX user reports conflict (Open, Sep 20, 2026; Obstructed, May 17, 2025) and are not official, so no access level is recorded. The remains claim comes from one trail-app listing and needs confirmation before publication.
